content.text: Digital creators in regions restricted from using platforms like Stripe face significant barriers when building an online store. In countries like Nigeria or Venezuela, conventional [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/why-payment-infrastructure-south-asian-creators-keeps-failing-2|COREMERCH guide to payment]] systems often fail, leaving creators without a viable way to monetize their work. This guide will walk you through [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/setting-up-nowpayments-digital-store-step-step-deployment-7|setting]] up a crypto store using [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/cloudflare-r2-digital-product-storage-delivery-explained-digital-14|Cloudflare R2]] Pages, ensuring you have full ownership and control over your digital products and transactions.
Why This Infrastructure Works When Platforms Fail

The primary advantage of using infrastructure like Cloudflare Pages is that it circumvents the limitations of conventional payment processors. Unlike platforms that impose geographical restrictions, this setup empowers creators by allowing them to leverage blockchain technology. By utilizing crypto payment systems, you ensure that transactions can occur instantly and securely without the need for intermediaries. This model provides not only sovereignty over your assets but also resilience against financial isolation, making it an ideal solution for those in regions with unstable economic conditions.
What You Need Before You Deploy

To successfully deploy your crypto store on Cloudflare Pages, you need a few critical components. First, set up a Cloudflare account for hosting your site. Next, prepare your digital products, ensuring they are ready for delivery. You'll also need a NOWPayments account to handle crypto transactions seamlessly. Familiarize yourself with Supabase for data management and Google Apps Script for handling backend logic. These tools work together to create a robust framework that supports your store's operations from the ground up, ensuring you can focus on selling your products.
Setting Up Your Payment and Delivery Pipeline

To establish a smooth payment and delivery pipeline, begin by integrating NOWPayments with your Cloudflare Pages setup. This involves configuring your payment buttons to link directly to your products. After securing the payment integration, set up a file delivery mechanism using Google Drive or Cloudflare R2, ensuring that purchased digital products are delivered automatically upon confirmation of payment. This streamlined process minimizes delays, enhancing customer satisfaction and trust. Testing the entire flow on the mainnet will confirm that your payment processing works flawlessly before going live.
Own your infrastructure; don’t rent it.
Going Live and Processing Your First Transaction

Once your infrastructure is set up and tested, it's time to launch your store. Promote your products across social media and relevant platforms, ensuring your target audience knows where to find you. Monitor the transactions closely during the initial phase to address any unforeseen issues promptly. Use analytics to gather data on customer interactions and sales patterns. By focusing on the customer experience and responding to feedback, you can refine your offerings and enhance your store's performance as it grows.
Scaling Once the Infrastructure Is Running

After successfully processing your first transactions, you can begin scaling your operations. Start by adding more digital products to your store, leveraging the capabilities of your established infrastructure. Use the data collected during the initial launch to optimize your marketing strategies, targeting your efforts more effectively. Consider exploring the Edge Commerce Stack from COREMERCH for advanced features such as SPF/DKIM/DMARC configurations and enhanced data management through Supabase. This stack will support your growth by providing a robust foundation as your business expands.

The difference between Stack 01 and Stack 02 is not which one works — both work — it is which one fits your situation. Stack 01 is the right choice if you want to deploy yourself, you are comfortable with Google Workspace tools, and your initial volume is under 100 orders per day. The Sovereign Blueprint at $47 documents the complete Stack 01 build with full source code and step-by-step configuration. Stack 02 is the right choice if you want the deployment done for you, you need higher volume capacity, or you want email deliverability infrastructure configured from day one. The Edge Commerce Stack at $197 has COREMERCH deploy Stack 02 under your accounts in 48 hours, end-to-end tested before handoff. Both are available at https://coremerch.github.io/products.html.
No subscriptions, just lifetime access.

The setup decision comes down to time versus depth. The Sovereign Blueprint at $47 gives you everything to build Stack 01 yourself in an afternoon or Stack 02 over a weekend — full source code, step-by-step configuration, and the NOWPayments integration guide. The Edge Commerce Stack at $197 has COREMERCH build Stack 02 for you in 48 hours, end-to-end tested before handoff, with SPF, DKIM, and DMARC configured for email deliverability. Both paths lead to a store you own completely. Both are at https://coremerch.github.io/products.html.
Your Deployment Checklist

Read the Sovereign Blueprint before you start configuring anything — understanding the complete architecture before touching any settings prevents the most common configuration mistakes. Create all required accounts first: NOWPayments, Cloudflare or GitHub, Supabase or Google account, Resend or Gmail. Then configure the backend with all credentials before deploying it. Then deploy the backend and confirm the endpoint is live. Then configure NOWPayments with the endpoint URL. Then build and deploy the storefront. Then configure your custom domain if using one. Then run the mainnet test. Then check the order database. Then — and only then — share the URL. The sequence is not arbitrary. Each step depends on the previous one.

NOWPayments charges a 0.5% fee on all transactions with no KYC requirements. This is significantly lower than many conventional payment processors, making it an attractive option for crypto transactions.
